svg.title: Two ways to flatten the Kosmos: gross and subtle reductionism on the four quadrants
svg.desc: Three two-by-two quadrant grids side by side, interior on the left and exterior on the right of each. The first is the Kosmos: all four windows filled, I, It, We, Its, with a thought at the crossing. The second is gross reductionism: three windows are empty dotted outlines with arrows into the Upper Right, which now holds only scattered dots labelled atoms. The third is subtle reductionism: the two interior windows are empty dotted outlines, arrows carry I to It and We to Its, and the exterior half holds one web of connected nodes labelled the great interlocking web; the purple interior tint is gone. Under each grid, Wilber's verdict: gross reductionism has not been historically that influential; subtle reductionism is the truly devastating contributor to modern flatland ontology. Below, two verbatim passages from Sex, Ecology, Spirituality chapter 4.
svg.text: WILBER WIKI · A CONCEPT IN ONE PICTURE
Two ways to flatten the Kosmos
The atomist keeps only atoms. The holist keeps the whole web and loses every within. Wilber says the second built flatland.
one thought, four windows: interiors and exteriors, all four real
every interior has an exterior correlate,
which is what makes both reductions tempting
dependent upon, but not reducible to, the others.”

g.text: all quadrants to the Upper Right, then the Upper Right to atoms

g.text: nothing but atoms: no interiors anywhere,
yet not, in Wilber’s telling, the main story
“…by and large it has not been
the Left half collapsed to its correlates on the Right half

g.text: the web is kept whole and every within is gone:
a holism of surfaces, with nothing inside it
◇ The three grids, the dotted empties, the arrows and the web drawing are this wiki’s; the two reductionisms, their moves, their verdicts and their targets are Wilber’s
“They don’t reduce everything to atoms; they reduce everything in the Left-Hand
to a Right-Hand description in the ‘system.’ They reduce a four-quadrant holism
(or Kosmic holism) to merely a Right-Hand holism, a flatland holism.”
Ken Wilber, Sex, Ecology, Spirituality (1995), ch. 4
“…the downside of the Enlightenment was that it took a Kosmos of both Left and
Right dimensions and reduced it to a cosmos that could be empirically (or
monologically) described: it collapsed the Left half to its correlates on the Right
half. Its great crime was not gross reductionism but subtle reductionism.”
Ken Wilber, Sex, Ecology, Spirituality (1995), ch. 4
Redrawn from Wilber’s account of gross and subtle reductionism in SES ch. 4; not a reproduction of a published figure.
The quadrant frame follows “One thought, four windows” · sans labels summarise SES ch. 4 · ◇ marks this wiki’s own device
